claims.text: MongoDB 8.0 documents checkpoint recovery for an interrupted replica-set index build after a clean shutdown with force:true or SIGTERM when quorum is "votingMembers". That setting does not make a crash resumable: the documented crash path restarts the build from the beginning. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

For the two-phase build path, the server design lists a voting replica-set member, literal commit quorum "votingMembers", and enabled majority read concern as general resumability prerequisites. A numerically equivalent quorum or "majority" must not be assumed to preserve resumability merely because the same members happen to satisfy it. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

A missing data-bearing voter can leave a default-quorum build waiting even when an election majority remains available. Percona demonstrated this in a three-voter set: the default waited for the third node, whereas a separate build using "majority" completed with two nodes available. (high confidence)

SERVER-124042 reports a rolling-restart race: quorum appeared satisfied although a returning secondary restarted its uncommitted build. The issue lists no affected or fixed versions, so it cannot establish exposure for a particular release. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-27)

A member with buildIndexes:false cannot participate in a commit quorum. The current command reference says "votingMembers" cannot be used if any voting node has buildIndexes:false; operators must change that configuration or choose another quorum. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Lowering commit quorum can let the primary commit before a slow secondary is ready. When that secondary reaches commitIndexBuild, oplog application can stall until its local build finishes. Quorum controls readiness coordination and does not replace write concern. (high confidence)

The master-branch server design also describes a primary-driven index-build path that replicates internal index writes and has no commit-quorum concept. The "votingMembers" resumability rule should therefore be scoped to simultaneous two-phase builds rather than presented as a universal rule for every index-build architecture. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

For simultaneous two-phase index builds, commitQuorum gates the primary commit on readiness reports, including the primary itself. The default "votingMembers" requires all voting data-bearing members; it is distinct from "majority" and excludes arbiters and non-voting data-bearing members. (high confidence)

The server design additionally requires a voting member and majority read concern for two-phase resumability. It waits for the majority commit point before scanning, after installing side-write interception. (low confidence)

A missing data-bearing voter can leave a votingMembers build waiting even with a healthy election majority. Percona reproduced this on 4.4.22-21: the index appeared in getIndexes but was unavailable to the query planner until the missing voter returned. (medium confidence)

setIndexCommitQuorum can change a running build to majority. For a createIndexes operation building several indexes together, indexNames must identify the entire group belonging to that builder. (medium confidence)

Lowering quorum trades readiness coverage for earlier primary commit: a secondary that has not finished can block oplog application upon receiving commitIndexBuild. A smaller quorum does not restrict which members build the index. (medium confidence)

Starting in MongoDB 8.0, post-commit write concern waits for the specified nodes to replicate the index-build oplog entry; earlier releases waited for those nodes to finish the index build. Do not interpret command success as proof that every secondary index is usable. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The MongoDB 8.0 manual allows checkpoint resumption only once for a given build. A further restart during that build starts it from the beginning; votingMembers alone is therefore insufficient to guarantee repeated checkpoint recovery. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Members vote after scanning their collection and performing the first side-write drain. While waiting for the commit decision they continue handling side writes. After quorum, the primary checks remaining constraints and replicates either commitIndexBuild or abortIndexBuild. (high confidence)

setIndexCommitQuorum changes the requirement of an in-progress build. Its indexNames array must include the entire group built by the same createIndexes operation. It has no effect on a build started with quorum 0. (medium confidence)
